lead: Scent layering is the practice of using matching or complementary scented products, such as body wash, lotion and fragrance, in sequence so that the smell builds, lasts longer and reads as a single signature. People use it to smell consistently good through a whole day, which looksmaxxing communities treat as part of overall presentation and attractiveness.[2]

The fragrance industry promotes a version of the technique: scented bath oil, shower gel or lotion in the morning, a lighter eau de toilette in the afternoon, and perfume at pulse points in the evening.[1] Some enthusiasts go further and blend several fragrances or fragrance oils; one looksmax.org user asked how to reproduce results a forum guide author attributed to blending popular designer scents.[3]

Reference sources say wear time depends on concentration, with cologne lasting around 2 hours, eau de toilette 2 to 4 and perfume up to 6 to 8, and that drier skin holds fragrance for less time than skin with more oil.[1] That is the rationale behind pairing a scent with a moisturising lotion. No published trials have tested layering itself.

paras: Layering means building a scent in steps. A scented wash leaves a faint base on the skin, a lotion from the same line seals it in, and a fragrance in the same family sits on top. Industry guidance describes a lighter or heavier scent through the day as another form of layering.[1]

Wikipedia lists approximate aromatic-compound levels of 15 to 30 percent for parfum, 15 to 20 percent for eau de parfum, 5 to 15 percent for eau de toilette and 2 to 3 percent for eau de cologne, and notes that dilutions vary between houses.[1] Layering is often described as a way to extend the shorter-lasting, lighter concentrations.

The same reference says dry skin does not hold fragrance as long as skin with more oil, that hydration can affect how long a scent lasts, and that diet and medications can change how a scent smells on a given wearer.[1] Proponents use these points to explain why a lotion is part of the routine.

Fragrance is a regular topic on looksmax.org, where users ask for recommendations and trade favourite colognes.[2] Blending is also discussed: one thread asks how to replicate a layered fragrance approach described in a facial-improvement guide, listing designer scents and replica oils the poster owns.[3]

Natural and synthetic perfume materials include compounds that can cause allergic reactions, and a long history of use does not by itself establish safety.[1] Stacking several scented products increases the number of fragrance ingredients in contact with skin.

lore.intro: Layering is discussed as a way to make a scent last and read as deliberate, often alongside fragrance recommendations and blending experiments.[2][3]

claims.claim: Matching body wash, lotion and fragrance makes a scent last longer
claims.believers: Proponents say a consistent base builds the scent and leaves skin moisturised, so the top fragrance holds.[1]
claims.experts: Reference sources note hydrated skin holds fragrance longer than dry skin;[1] no studies of layering itself have been published.

claims.claim: Blending several fragrances produces a stronger, more attractive signature
claims.believers: A looksmax.org thread describes attempts to copy blends credited to a forum guide author, using several designer scents and replica oils.[3]
claims.experts: No published study has tested blended fragrances for attractiveness.

name: Scent layering (body wash, lotion, fragrance)

card.summary: Stacking matched wash, lotion and fragrance to make a scent last; popular, untested.
card.note: More scented products means more potential allergens.

quick.overview:
Scent layering uses products from the same scent family, such as body wash, lotion and fragrance, so the smell lasts and feels coherent.

The fragrance industry itself suggests layering through the day.
quick.mechanism: Moisturised skin is said to hold fragrance longer, and a matching base reinforces the top scent.
quick.risks: Fragrance ingredients can be allergenic; no layering-specific studies were found.
